hook: SCP-3002 arrives as a forwarded email, and each later version of the file comes wrapped in another message from someone higher up. The first report is small and quiet: a childhood memory that most of a prison's inmates turn out to share. Read the emails as carefully as the reports, because a second story is being told in them.
whyItMatters: It uses a chain of revisions to stage a slow apocalypse, with the same item reclassified from Safe to Euclid to Keter as the Foundation keeps underestimating it. The article's real subject is the Foundation's own conduct, which the later versions drag into the open. It shows how much story the plain apparatus of headers, logs and cover emails can carry when the reader is invited to look between them.
thingsToNotice:
The memory changes character from version to version: a vivid shared day in the woods, then something people defend as their own, then an intelligence that edits files, rewrites a RAISA officer's loyalties and, by the end, overrides bodies so crowds converge to infect anyone still clean. The girl at its center, Lily Veselka, keeps asking whether you remember her and whether the project is finished, and those questions turn painful once the abandoned Site-E is found in Ukraine. A burnt letter from O5-2 describes Project Lethe, a mass memory-control tool built on a single girl kept for invasive brain surgery while conscious, who stopped answering to her name, harmed herself and tried to kill herself with a sharpened utensil, while the writer proposes replacing her with a trigger planted in nearly all of humanity.

The email senders' worry shifts from side effects to covering their tracks; O5-2 even sends someone to clean up what is left of the project. In the final version 78 percent of humanity is contaminated and the Foundation pleads with other groups, getting silence, destroyed replies and a few bleak notes. Command votes down every drastic option, and Veles, the O5 the Lethe letter was addressed to, refuses to reopen the project and orders the termination of the doctor who suggests it, so the shrinking vote counts and the blank field after a proposal simply titled Restart leave you unsure whether anyone uncompromised is still deciding.

related.note: Proposed in the final document as a way to repopulate Earth, and turned down.
